# Arithmetic reciprocal assembly inherits high off-axis zeros

STATUS: ANALYTIC_PAPER_CANDIDATE awaiting exact independent review.
Base: ae905d0b8e290f500303f8f141e8ba4cc5e0a238. Isolated research.
Original full V and RH remain OPEN; no original-source negative witness.

## Bounded question and prior scope

The accepted MELLINEDGE result concerns the raw finite Mellin transforms,
and explicitly does not classify zeros of the reciprocal assemblies.
The arithmetic assembly report proves an exact positive even source,
convergence to full Phi, and an exact sum of two reflected Mellin terms;
its zero question is left open. This note checks that exact sum. It does
not reopen generic SUPPORT, Pick, or the geometric gamma family.

Inputs read in full, with byte pins in the adjacent private manifest:

1. REPORT_2026-09-15_ARITHMETIC_RECIPROCITY.md, AR1--AR4.
2. REPORT_2026-09-16_MELLINEDGE_COFINAL_OBSTRUCTION.md, C0--C5.

We inherit their already accepted source bounds, prime-torus construction
and convergence proofs; we do not claim a new independent audit of all
those earlier results. The NEW step is the uniform estimate for the
reflected term in the complete assembled transform, followed by Rouche.

The only additional published analytic input is the vertical-strip gamma
asymptotic, NIST DLMF 5.11.9, https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.11.E9 . It follows
from the sectorial Stirling expansion 5.11.3 and is uniform when the real
part ranges in a fixed bounded interval. The two gamma arguments below
have exactly opposite imaginary parts; their exponential factors cancel
in the ratio. No estimate uniform in N is required or asserted.

## A1. Source and exact assembled transform

Let T_N be the sum of independent Gamma(2,rate pi*n^2), 1<=n<=N,
and let r_N be its density. Put kappa=5/2, c=kappa/2=5/4, and

    a_N(x)=exp(5x/2)r_N(exp(2x)),
    H_N(x)=[a_N(x)+a_N(-x)]/2,
    M_N(s)=E[T_N^(s-1)].

The normalized Fourier transform of H_N, in its defining strip, is

    A_N(z)=[M_N(c-iz/2)+M_N(c+iz/2)]/[2 M_N(c)].       (A1)

The denominator M_N(c) is strictly positive. The ordinary integral for
A_N is holomorphic for |Im z|<4N+1/2. Define

    B_N(w)=M_N(w)+M_N(kappa-w).                       (A2)

At w=c-iz/2 the numerator in A1 is exactly B_N(w). In particular

    z=2i(w-c).                                       (A3)

No replacement by the sign, modulus, or just one of the summands is made.

For 0<Re w<kappa, both Mellin terms admit the accepted exact formula

    M_N(w)=4 pi^(1-w)Gamma(w) D_N(w),
    D_N(w)=sum_(n=1)^N w_Nn n^(2-2w)(w+d_Nn),
    w_Nn=(N!)^4/[(N-n)!^2(N+n)!^2],
    d_Nn=n(H_(N+n)-H_(N-n))-3/2.                     (A4)

H_k in A4 denotes a harmonic number, not the source H_N(x). All finite
harmonic corrections and all composite-prime phase dependencies remain
in D_N. The real log is used for powers of positive pi and n.

## A2. Accepted prime-torus limit, with N fixed first

For every sufficiently large fixed N, the accepted C1--C4 construct unit
phases zeta_p for primes p<=N and real tau_j tending to +infinity such that

    P_N(s)=sum_(n=1)^N w_Nn n^(2-2s)
                     product_(p<=N) zeta_p^v_p(n),
    P_N(11/8)=0,
    D_N(s+i tau_j)/(i tau_j) -> P_N(s)                (A5)

locally uniformly in s. P_N is entire and not identically zero because
P_N(s) tends to w_N1>0 as real s tends to +infinity. In the earlier proof,
unique factorization supplied the allowed phases and the unconditional
prime-count law supplied the requisite mass split. Both are inherited.

Choose a closed disk K centered at sigma_0=11/8 with radius delta<1/32.
It lies strictly inside c<Re s<kappa. The radius can be chosen so that
P_N has no zero on its boundary. Multiple interior zeros are allowed.

## A3. The reflected term vanishes in the same normalization

On a neighborhood of K and for sufficiently large tau>0 define

    F_(N,tau)(s)= B_N(s+i tau)
                  /[4 pi^(1-s-i tau)Gamma(s+i tau) i tau].       (A6)

The normalizing factor is holomorphic, finite and nonzero there. Direct
substitution of BOTH terms of A4 gives the exact identity

    F_(N,tau)(s)=D_N(s+i tau)/(i tau)
                  +G_tau(s) D_N(kappa-s-i tau)/(i tau),
    G_tau(s)=pi^(2s+2i tau-kappa)
                  Gamma(kappa-s-i tau)/Gamma(s+i tau).         (A7)

For s=sigma+iv in K, put y=tau+v>0. The real parts of the two gamma
arguments are kappa-sigma and sigma; the imaginary parts are -y and y.
The uniform vertical-strip gamma asymptotic therefore gives

    |G_tau(s)|=pi^(2sigma-kappa)
                    y^(kappa-2sigma)[1+o(1)],                 (A8)

uniformly on K. Since sigma>=11/8-delta, kappa-2sigma<=-1/4+2delta
<-3/16. Thus sup_K |G_tau|=O_K(tau^(-3/16)).

Also, for fixed N, the finite formula A4 gives directly

    sup_(s in K) |D_N(kappa-s-i tau)| <= C_(N,K)(1+tau).        (A9)

Indeed every n^(2-2(kappa-s-i tau)) has modulus bounded on K independently
of tau, and every linear factor is bounded by tau plus a fixed constant.
No independent choice of the reflected prime phases is made or needed.

Combining A7--A9 and the actual sequence from A5 proves

    F_(N,tau_j)(s) -> P_N(s), locally uniformly on K.            (A10)

This establishes a strict perturbation estimate on the boundary of K.
It does NOT say B_N vanishes at the old raw M_N zeros, nor compare a
perturbation to a vanishing leading term at a single point.

## A4. Zeros of the full assembled transform

The minimum of |P_N| on the chosen boundary is positive. For all sufficiently
large j, A10 and Rouche give a zero s_j of F_(N,tau_j) in K. The nonzero
normalizing factor implies B_N(s_j+i tau_j)=0. A1--A3 then give

    z_j=2i(s_j+i tau_j-c),       A_N(z_j)=0.                    (A11)

Their real parts tend to -infinity and

    |Im z_j-1/4| < 2delta < 1/16.

In particular these zeros lie strictly inside 0<Im z<1/2, and also inside
the defining Fourier strip for every N>=1. This is not a conclusion from
meromorphic continuation beyond the integral's domain.

Using successively shrinking zero-free circles about sigma_0 and a diagonal
subsequence of arbitrarily large recurrence times strengthens this to

    Re z_j -> -infinity,       Im z_j -> 1/4.                   (A12)

Evenness and reality of H_N imply A_N(-z)=A_N(z) and
A_N(conjugate(z))=conjugate(A_N(z)). Consequently there are corresponding
zeros at unbounded positive real parts and near both Im z=+1/4 and -1/4.
These symmetries do not need an additional independent phase selection.

Therefore, for EVERY sufficiently large N, the actual arithmetic reciprocal
transform A_N has infinitely many off-real zeros within |Im z|<1/2. No
unbounded subsequence of this particular finite family can be zero-free
throughout the punctured critical strip at every horizontal height.

## A5. Exact boundary of the conclusion

The raw MELLINEDGE report alone did not classify the zeros of H_N's
transform. A3--A4 now pay the missing reflected-term estimate. Positive
evenness obtained by arithmetic reciprocal assembly does not remove those
high zeros. This is a new corollary for that already specified approximation,
not a new proof of the original sign and not a newly discovered prime theorem.

The quantifier order remains: first fix a sufficiently large N, then let
the recurrence heights tend to infinity. The proof gives no uniform-in-N
height, no fixed compact containing such zeros for infinitely many N, and
no first failing numerical N. The accepted convergence A_N -> normalized
xi on each fixed horizontal strip is compatible with zeros escaping to
infinity: it is absolute convergence, with no positive lower bound on the
tiny limiting transform at all large horizontal heights.

In particular the weaker compact-by-compact eventual zero-exclusion
condition (for each fixed R and epsilon) is not refuted by A12. That
condition for this family would still require proof; no new generic request
to prove it is opened here. The geometric square-root assembly is distinct
and its previously proved central slab remains unchanged.

This does not alter the full density r, original f, interval I, full V,
boundary terms, or any complex-family quantifier. No negative row of the
original V is obtained. Actual RH, full V, Pick and global VAR remain open.
The bounded decision is to reject global finite-level zero exclusion for
the arithmetic assembly too; preserve its convergence and exact formulas.
No source-sign counter reset, canonical admission, or production mutation.

AUTOPSY: dropped=COUPLING; note=Exact arithmetic reciprocal assembly retains high finite-level zeros because the reflected Mellin term is uniformly smaller in the prime-torus normalization; compact limiting zero exclusion and original full-source sign remain open.

# Independent arithmetic MELLINEDGE review

**Verdict: ACCEPT_ARITHMETIC_RECIPROCAL_ASSEMBLY_HIGH_ZERO_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.**

Complete candidate reviewed: `ARITHMETIC_MELLINEDGE_CANDIDATE.md`, SHA256 `a3d0baea3825b966d3ae9a115f862286618e001c51d424f64b0bbcef50c74532`, 8739 bytes. Complete manifest read: `ARITHMETIC_MELLINEDGE_PINS.json`, SHA256 `ed8e38b3136614f2ef53e0cbdbd1b8cd0bcb90849395489ace626d0efcbbb43c`. A1–A5 pass within the stated quantifier order and scope. No correction is required.

The new accepted corollary is: for every sufficiently large fixed N, the exact arithmetic reciprocal assembly A_N has infinitely many off-real zeros in its defining Fourier domain, with an unbounded sequence of real parts and imaginary parts approaching 1/4 (and the symmetry-related sequences). This rejects global finite-level zero exclusion for this particular arithmetic family. It proves neither a zero of the limiting xi off its critical line nor the sign of original V.

## 1. Startup, sources and dependency boundary

The canonical compact `python3 orchestrator/workflow_runtime.py plan` was run first after reading the entry instructions. It returned exit 2, ACTIVE control with no fatal errors, read-only production HOLD, foreign ownership and `writes_performed:false`. No recovery, selection, canonical mutation or dispatch was attempted. The isolated research checkout was verified clean at `ae905d0b8e290f500303f8f141e8ba4cc5e0a238`.

Both named mathematical reports were read completely and their hashes checked directly:

- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-15_ARITHMETIC_RECIPROCITY.md`: `b128c925d794693fdbc5b1e8257e5587060c92d60770a650f2f8d26ee6838f53`, 5011 bytes. AR1–AR4 establish the source, its integral strip, normalization, exact reflected Mellin sum, and convergence.
- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-16_MELLINEDGE_COFINAL_OBSTRUCTION.md`: `5748be3691ff3308ae700a9697046bbdd3ef4d688cb36cabd0d4c21836319129`, 11529 bytes. Its independent acceptance records C0–C5 for the raw Mellin family. It supplies the exact finite formula, the fixed-N prime-torus zero and the unbounded positive-time recurrence sequence.
- `orchestrator/state/CHANNEL_RUNTIME.json`: `f7bb8eed28bf9b67292f67bbbdde96cecb4baf42e758e0acbb4be34d5baa6418`; checked only for the manifest's byte consistency. This is not a proof premise or live dispatch authorization.

The prior reports' already accepted analytic source estimates and prime-mass construction are inherited; their complete proofs are not claimed independently re-audited here. In particular the old raw Mellin zero theorem is not itself a theorem about the reflected sum. The present A3 estimate is necessary to bridge that distinction.

The one additional primary input was read directly at [NIST DLMF 5.11.9](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.11#E9), including the adjacent uniformity statement and the notes deriving it from 5.11.3. It gives the modulus asymptotic for gamma at large positive or negative imaginary part, uniformly when the real part is bounded. This is exactly the domain consumed below; no fixed-argument ratio theorem is misapplied to opposite imaginary directions. No new literature search or numerical source test was used.

## 2. A1: full-source normalization and domain

For a_N(x)=exp(5x/2)r_N(exp(2x)), substitute t=exp(2x), dx=dt/(2t). This gives

    integral a_N(x)exp(-izx)dx = (1/2)M_N(5/4-iz/2).

Reflection x to -x changes the sign of iz/2. Since H_N is half the sum, its unnormalized transform is one quarter of the sum of Mellin terms. Its mass is M_N(5/4)/2. Division therefore gives exactly A1 with denominator 2M_N(c), not M_N(c) or 4M_N(c). The denominator is strictly positive by the positive density and finiteness of that moment.

The small-t behavior r_N(t) of order t^(2N-1) requires Re s>1-2N for the Mellin integral. Applying this simultaneously to c-iz/2 and c+iz/2 gives |Im z|<4N+1/2. The inherited exponential upper tail pays the other endpoint. This is the ordinary holomorphic integral domain; it is enough for every zero constructed below. No meromorphic continuation outside that domain is being counted as an ordinary Fourier zero.

At w=c-iz/2, the reflected argument equals 5/2-w, and solving for z gives z=2i(w-c). The sign and factor 2 are correct. The finite formula A4 agrees term for term with accepted C0, including harmonic-number indices and the -3/2 constant. Although the single formula holds for Re w>0, its use for both summands in the stated strip 0<Re w<5/2 is legitimate. The normalization of X/Phi in the previous projects is not substituted for this finite sum.

## 3. A2: fixed-N prime-torus input

For each sufficiently large N, accepted C1–C4 supply phases indexed by primes, not independently by every integer n. Their products retain the valuations v_p(n), and the same phases arise as limits of exp(-2i tau_j log p) for a sequence tau_j tending to positive infinity. The exact finite sum then yields locally uniformly

    D_N(s+i tau_j)/(i tau_j) -> P_N(s).

The factors (s+i tau_j+d_Nn)/(i tau_j) tend to 1 for fixed N. Thus the harmonic corrections are present before the limit and their disappearance in this limit is justified, not a claim that they are identically absent or uniformly small as N increases.

The supplied equality P_N(11/8)=0 is exact. P_N is entire and nonzero as a function: on the positive real ray all n>=2 terms tend to zero, leaving w_N1>0. Its zeros are isolated. One can therefore choose arbitrarily small positive radii delta<1/32 around 11/8 avoiding zeros on the boundary, with a whole neighborhood still in c<Re s<5/2. No simplicity or transversality assumption on this complex zero is required.

## 4. A3: the new reflected-term estimate

Let w=s+i tau. Dividing the exact M_N(w)+M_N(5/2-w) by 4 pi^(1-w)Gamma(w)i tau gives precisely A7. In particular, the ratio of pi powers is pi^(2s+2i tau-5/2); no factor depending exponentially on tau is omitted.

For s=sigma+iv, the two gamma arguments are (5/2-sigma)-i(tau+v) and sigma+i(tau+v). Put y=tau+v. For tau large, y>0 uniformly on the compact disk. The real parts remain in fixed bounded positive intervals. In their gamma moduli the exp(-pi y/2) factors cancel exactly, as do the factors sqrt(2pi). The resulting ratio is

    |G_tau(s)| = pi^(2sigma-5/2) y^(5/2-2sigma)(1+o(1)),

uniformly on that disk. Since sigma>=11/8-delta, the exponent is at most -1/4+2delta<-3/16. Also y/tau tends uniformly to 1 and the remaining pi factor is bounded. Hence sup|G_tau|=O_K(tau^(-3/16)), as asserted. A modulus asymptotic suffices; no limiting complex phase for G_tau is assumed.

For the other factor, each finite term of D_N(5/2-s-i tau) has modulus bounded by

    w_Nn n^(-3+2sigma) [tau+|5/2-s+d_Nn|].

Summing over n<=N proves A9 with a finite constant depending on N and K. In particular the reflected phases remain those of the same tau; there is no independent choice or decoupling. The proof needs no cancellation at all in this reflected finite sum.

Dividing A9 by tau and using the preceding gamma bound makes the whole second term uniformly O_(N,K)(tau^(-3/16)). Combining this with the actual prime recurrence limit establishes A10. All estimates hold on a slightly larger neighborhood if needed, so the claimed local uniformity and subsequent contour argument are legitimate.

The normalizer in A6 is holomorphic, finite and nonzero near K: pi powers use the real logarithm, tau is a nonzero fixed real parameter, and Gamma(s+i tau) has neither zeros nor poles there. Both Mellin terms in B_N are holomorphic there as well. Zeros and their multiplicities are therefore preserved by division by this normalizer.

## 5. A4: Rouche, multiplicity and the coordinate map

On a chosen zero-free boundary circle, min|P_N| is positive. Uniform convergence makes |F_(N,tau_j)-P_N| smaller than that minimum for all sufficiently large j. Rouche consequently preserves the number of zeros in the disk, counted with multiplicity; this number is positive because the center is a zero. This establishes a zero of the full sum, not the unsupported claim that the old raw M_N zeros themselves remain fixed after adding a summand.

Write the resulting zero as w_j=s_j+i tau_j with s_j inside the disk. Then

    Re z_j = -2(tau_j+Im s_j) -> -infinity,
    Im z_j = 2(Re s_j-5/4),
    |Im z_j-1/4|<2delta<1/16.

Thus every such zero lies strictly in 0<Im z<1/2 and in the ordinary defining Fourier strip for each N>=1. Their unbounded real parts ensure infinitely many distinct zeros. By successively shrinking the zero-free circles and choosing recurrence times beyond each required threshold, one obtains the diagonal sequence with Im z_j tending to 1/4. This remains a fixed-N argument.

A real even integrable H_N gives both evenness and conjugation symmetry of A_N throughout the symmetric strip. The reflected zero sequences at positive real parts and at negative imaginary parts therefore follow without new prime-phase choices.

## 6. A5: exact exclusion scope

The conclusion is valid for every sufficiently large N. Therefore no unbounded subsequence of these finite arithmetic assemblies can satisfy zero exclusion at every horizontal height throughout the punctured critical strip. This is a new bounded corollary for the specified arithmetic reconstruction, supported by the new A3 perturbation bound in addition to the inherited raw Mellin result.

It gives no uniform recurrence height in N, no explicit first bad N, and no fixed compact containing zeros for infinitely many N. Neither the phase construction nor the constants in A9 or the required Rouche times supply such uniformity. In particular it does not refute eventual exclusion on each fixed compact separated from the real axis. The accepted uniform absolute convergence on each fixed horizontal strip remains compatible with these zeros escaping horizontally to infinity; it is not a relative error bound against a positive all-height lower bound for the limiting transform.

The actual full density and its Fourier transform, original V, and all original coefficient quantifiers are unchanged. There is no negative theta row, no actual Pick/global VAR conclusion and no RH conclusion. The geometric square-root family is distinct and is not addressed. No canonical admission or new source-sign counter value follows from this review.

Only the assigned private review file was written. Existing foreign files and production HOLD were preserved; no descendant, provider dispatch, new hunt, numerical campaign, Lean run or publication was undertaken.

Candidate SHA256: a3d0baea3825b966d3ae9a115f862286618e001c51d424f64b0bbcef50c74532.
Verdict: ACCEPT_ARITHMETIC_RECIPROCAL_ASSEMBLY_HIGH_ZERO_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.
The complete independent review was read; no correction was requested.
Review SHA256: 531db4103acc613e0b65d2e8e5ceb2b59ca37858aab67e36839ea0345b73845d.

I read the full arithmetic assembly and full C0-C5 cofinal raw-Mellin report.
With w=c-iz/2, kappa-w=c+iz/2, so 2 M_N(c) A_N(z)=B_N(w) exactly.
The denominator is a strictly positive real moment. Solving for z gives
2i(w-c), so a zero near w=11/8+i*tau has Im z near +1/4 and Re z near
-2*tau, not the other way around. The reflected point has real part near
9/8>0. Thus both raw A4 integral formulas and the Fourier integral domain
are valid; no continuation through a missing source domain is required.

Dividing B_N(w) by 4*pi^(1-w)*Gamma(w)*i*tau leaves D_N(w)/(i*tau)
and pi^(2w-kappa)*Gamma(kappa-w)/Gamma(w) times D_N(kappa-w)/(i*tau).
For w=s+i*tau the gamma imaginary parts are exactly opposite. DLMF 5.11.9,
including its explicit uniformity clause, was opened and read. The common
exp(-pi*abs(Im w)/2) cancels. The ratio power is kappa-2Re s, uniformly
negative in the selected disk. All finite harmonic terms in D_N are kept;
the reflected finite sum is O_N(tau). No control of its phase is necessary.

The original prime-torus construction gives locally uniform convergence of
the normalized first term to one fixed nonzero entire P_N vanishing at
11/8, separately for each large N. It is stronger than mere existence of
some raw zeros and supplies the boundary comparison actually needed here.
A zero-free small circle exists by isolated zeros; Rouche counts zeros of
the complete normalized sum there. The normalizer has no poles or zeros
on that neighborhood for large positive tau. Shrinking circles with a
diagonal sequence of recurrence times gives the stated imaginary limit.
Repeated high times yield distinct zeros. Source evenness/reality supply
reflected quartets without further prime-phase assignments.

The result excludes global all-height finite-level zero exclusion for this
arithmetic family. It does not exclude eventual exclusion on each fixed
compact, nor provide a uniform-in-N height. Weighted L1 convergence implies
absolute uniform convergence on strips, not relative convergence where xi
is small. Therefore neither RH nor original V sign changes. The geometric
family is not being substituted, and its central-slab theorem is retained.
This corollary does not add a new source-sign property or restart SUPPORT.
